about: Accuracy corpus: YouTube videos spoken in Arabic that carry a manual (uploader-provided) Arabic caption track. Found by scripts/fetch_corpus.py --discover (76 qualified), fetched through CaptionForge by --fetch into <id>/audio.mp3 + <id>/ref.srt (gitignored). Each clip is scored over [start, end] seconds, snapped to whole caption cues. type: report = narrated news report; talk = studio interview/analysis; dialect = mostly a spoken dialect; control = must produce no words. reference — what the caption track turned out to be when read (fetch_corpus.py --inspect), which decides what a score against it means: 'human' = a person's verbatim transcript (punctuated, standard spelling) — CER is accuracy; 'asr-style' = normalised spelling (no hamza, ه for ة), no punctuation, disfluencies kept, ~7 s cues — a broadcaster's recogniser, perhaps post-edited: CER is agreement with a strong in-domain system, its errors counted as ours; 'msa-rendering' = human, but dialect speech rendered into Modern Standard Arabic — CER is not accuracy at all, only STREAM GAP (stream vs offline against the same text) means something.
